messages.content: 你能估計2020年印度孟加拉虎的人口數量嗎？並將其與同年肯亞非洲象的估計人口數量進行比較，然後估計這兩種物種在各自國家的當前年份的人口數量嗎？

function.name: estimate_population
function.description: Estimate the population of a particular species in a given country. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

species.description: The species for which population needs to be estimated.

country.description: The country where the species lives.

year.description: The year for which population estimate is sought. Default is the current year.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Can you estimate the 2020 population of Bengal tigers in India and compare it with the estimated population of African elephants in Kenya in the same year, then estimate the populations of these two species in their respective countries in the current year?" So we need to call the function estimate_population twice: once for Bengal tiger in India for year 2020, once for African elephant in Kenya for year 2020. Then we need to estimate the populations for the current year (which is 2026). So we need to call estimate_population twice more: Bengal tiger in India for year 2026, African elephant in Kenya for year 2026.

We should do calls in order. We'll first call estimate_population for Bengal tiger in India year 2020. Then call estimate_population for African elephant in Kenya year 2020. Then call estimate_population for Bengal tiger in India year 2026. Then call estimate_population for African elephant in Kenya year 2026.

We need to output the results after each call. The function returns some value. We need to handle the responses. We'll do calls sequentially.
